instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: The job is to bleed the front and back brakes on a Segway Xyber e-bike to ensure reliable stopping power in city traffic. The procedure relies on verifying the correct fluid type from the lever stamp, flushing until the fluid is clean, and ensuring the lever is rock-solid and does not touch the handlebar.

draft.title: Segway Xyber Brake Bleed and Flush
disqualifiers: Brake lever pulls all the way to the handlebar grip
Any fluid wetness or weeping at hoses or fittings after bleeding
releases: Safe to ride in city traffic and on gravel

steps.title: Verify Fluid Type
steps.explanation: Mixing DOT fluid and mineral oil destroys the brake seals, leading to complete brake failure within a week.

fields.prompt: Take a clear photo of the fluid type stamp on the lever body or reservoir cap.
fields.guidance: The photo must clearly show the text specifying the fluid type (e.g., 'Mineral Oil' or 'DOT') stamped on the brake hardware.

fields.prompt: Enter the exact type of brake fluid you are refilling with.
fields.acceptance_target: lever body or reservoir cap stamp
fields.guidance: The fluid type entered must exactly match the stamp on the lever body or reservoir cap.

steps.title: Flush and Bleed System
steps.explanation: Flushing replaces old, degraded fluid and expels trapped air bubbles that cause a spongy lever.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the discharged old fluid next to a sample of the fresh fluid.
fields.guidance: The photo must show both the old fluid container and new fluid container side-by-side to confirm a complete flush.

steps.title: Verify Lever Firmness
steps.explanation: A spongy lever or one that pulls to the bar means air is still in the system, which can cause brake failure under hard braking.

fields.prompt: Squeeze the brake lever hard. Does it pull all the way back to touch the handlebar grip?
fields.guidance: The lever must feel rock-solid and stop completely before contacting the handlebar grip.

steps.title: Inspect for Leaks
steps.explanation: Any fluid weeping from fittings or hoses will lead to pressure loss and contaminated brake pads.

fields.prompt: Inspect all hoses, fittings, and bleed ports by eye and touch. Is there any wetness or weeping fluid?
fields.guidance: All connections must be completely dry to the touch and show no signs of fluid weeping.
